title: Exact Value of Λ(zⁿ − 1) as a Function of n

problemStatement.formal: \Lambda(z^n - 1) = \max_C \operatorname{length}(\partial C) \text{ over connected components } C \text{ of } \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z^n - 1| < 1\}. \text{ Known: } \Lambda(z^n - 1) \to 2 \text{ as } n \to \infty \text{ and } \Lambda(z^n - 1) > 2 \text{ for all } n. \text{ Open: a closed-form expression for } n \mapsto \Lambda(z^n - 1), \text{ conjecturally a complete elliptic integral of a modulus depending on } n.
problemStatement.plain: The roots of z^n − 1 are the n equally-spaced nth roots of unity, and the region |z^n − 1| < 1 splits into n identical petals. We want the boundary length of one petal (the largest component) as an explicit function of n. It is known to shrink toward 2 as n grows, but no exact formula is known — and the exact value is conjectured to require elliptic integrals rather than elementary functions.
whyMatters: Tang resolved Erdős Problem #1044 asymptotically (inf Λ = 2 via the z^n − 1 family); an exact per-n formula would quantify how fast the infimum is approached and test the conjecture that z^n − 1 minimizes Λ at each degree.

It would give the first exact metric formula for a natural family of polynomial lemniscates, connecting to potential theory, transfinite diameter, and the classical Erdős–Herzog–Piranian study of level sets.

knownResults: Λ(z^n − 1) → 2 as n → ∞ and Λ(f) > 2 for all f (Tang's theorem, parent proof erdos-1044).
The sublevel set {|z^n − 1| < 1} has n-fold symmetry and consists of n congruent petals, so Λ equals one petal's perimeter.
references: P. Erdős, F. Herzog, G. Piranian, Metric properties of polynomials, J. Analyse Math. 6 (1958), 125-148.
Q. Tang, resolution of Erdős Problem #1044, https://erdosproblems.com/1044
